question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #16: A distributed deep learning model serving endpoint experienced severe throughput degradation and GPU memory fragmentation in Deep Learning Architectures (CNN, RNN, Transformers). During sustained peak inference, memory utilization hit 98% with OOM aborts specifically during 'Positional Encodings (Sinusoidal, RoPE, ALiBi)' execution.

### Engineering Challenge:
What is the optimal MLOps and architectural resolution to eliminate OOMs and optimize serving throughput for 'Positional Encodings (Sinusoidal, RoPE, ALiBi)'?

options.text: Allocate a static contiguous GPU VRAM tensor buffer sized to maximum possible sequence length for every incoming request.
Disable model pipelining and force all transformer attention heads onto host system RAM via CPU swap.
Retrain the model from scratch using a single linear feedforward layer to bypass attention.
Implement dynamic batching with continuous paged KV-cache management (PagedAttention) and FP16/INT8 activation quantization.

answer_explanation: In Deep Learning Architectures (CNN, RNN, Transformers), static allocation for sequence generation creates massive memory fragmentation. Continuous paged KV-cache allocation (such as vLLM) partitions key-value memory into non-contiguous blocks, slashing memory waste and preventing OOMs while maximizing concurrent throughput.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option D. Rationale: In Deep Learning Architectures (CNN, RNN, Transformers), static allocation for sequence generation creates massive memory fragmentation. Continuous paged KV-cache allocation (such as vLLM) partitions key-value memory into non-contiguous blocks, slashing memory waste and preventing OOMs while maximizing concurrent throughput.
